subject: Hospitality
title: Food Cost Percentages
description: A fast breakdown of Food Cost Percentages for builders.

hook.text: A restaurant's food cost—ingredients as a percentage of menu price—typically runs 28–35%. Go higher and profits vanish.

buildup.text: If a steak costs $10 in ingredients, it sells for $30–35. The rest covers labor, rent, utilities, and slim profit.

discovery.text: Pasta and pizza have the lowest food costs—often under 20%. That's why Italian restaurants can survive on lower prices.

twist.text: Drinks are the real moneymaker. A cocktail might cost $2 in ingredients and sell for $15. Bars subsidize kitchens.

climax.text: Menu pricing is a balancing act between food cost, perceived value, and what competitors charge. It's part math, part psychology.

punchline.text: The plate is 30% ingredient, 70% everything else. Margins are razor-thin.

quiz.question: Why are drinks so profitable compared to food?
options: Drink ingredients cost very little relative to their selling price
